messages.content: Write a page comparing a managed database service with running your own, for a technical audience choosing between them. Around 250 words.

# Managed Postgres, or run your own?

Most teams should start managed and stay managed. The interesting question is what you're actually buying, and when it stops being worth the markup.

What you buy is someone else's pager. RDS, Cloud SQL, and Neon handle minor-version patching, automated backups with point-in-time recovery, failover to a standby, and the storage layer underneath all of it. That last one matters more than people expect. Replacing a dying disk at 3 a.m. is not a skill most teams should be building.

The price is roughly 2-4x the raw compute, plus some real constraints. No superuser. Extension allowlists, so pgvector or TimescaleDB arrives when your provider decides it does. Slow-query logs behind a console you don't control. Major-version upgrades on the vendor's calendar rather than yours.

Running it yourself gets all of that back and hands you the bill in headcount instead. Someone owns connection pooling, WAL archiving to object storage, restore drills that actually run, and monitoring that pages before the disk fills. Call it a fraction of one SRE at steady state, plus a bad week whenever the primary dies. That is cheaper than a managed bill north of $10-15k a month, which is why the crossover shows up at scale and not at the start.

Two cases genuinely favor self-hosting: you need an extension or kernel-level tuning your provider won't support, or your data can't leave hardware you control.

Everything else is preference. Pick managed, write down the number at which you'd revisit the decision, and go build the product.

---

253 words. It takes a side rather than laying out a neutral matrix — say the word if you'd rather it stayed even-handed. The cost figures are illustrative order-of-magnitude, not quoted pricing; swap in your own numbers before this goes anywhere real. Clean pass on the repo's own `slopwatch` gate.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
# Managed Postgres, or run your own?

Start managed and stay there. The question worth arguing about is what the markup buys, and at what point it stops paying for itself.

Mainly it buys someone else's pager. RDS, Cloud SQL, and Neon take on minor-version patching, automated backups with point-in-time recovery, failover to a standby, and the storage layer holding all of it up. That last piece carries more weight than teams expect. Swapping a failing disk at 3 a.m. is not a muscle worth developing in-house.

You pay roughly 2-4x raw compute for it, and you accept limits. No superuser. Extension allowlists, so pgvector or TimescaleDB shows up when the vendor says so. Slow-query logs living in a console you don't own. Major upgrades scheduled on their calendar.

Self-hosting returns every one of those and bills you in headcount instead. Somebody has to own connection pooling, WAL archiving to object storage, restore drills that get run for real, and alerting that fires before the volume fills. Budget a slice of one SRE while things are calm, plus one miserable week each time a primary dies. Set against a managed invoice past $10-15k a month, the math flips, which is why the crossover lands at scale rather than on day one.

Two situations honestly favor rolling your own: you need an extension or kernel tuning the vendor won't allow, or the data legally cannot sit on hardware you don't control.

The rest is taste. Go managed, record the number that would make you reconsider, and ship the product.
